note: The run. One act per glyph family, taught in the order the rules depend on them. Every level carries its board, written out as rows of three-character cells (see `parseBoard` in src/board.js), and states the swaps it allows. A level has a right answer: `target` is what that answer activates, and exactly one line of swaps reaches it. `node tools/puzzleBoards.js` finds the colouring that makes a layout into such a board, and `node tools/makeLevels.js` checks every shipped level for the answer and for rival ones. `budget` here is the default for a level that states none.

levels.teaches: A glyph landing on its own colour activates
levels.note: Two pieces and one swap, and it is the right one. Nothing here can be done wrong.

levels.teaches: Any two cells swap — they need not touch
levels.note: The same pair at opposite corners. The move that was obvious is now the move that proves reach.

levels.teaches: Read both ends of a swap: what lands, and what it lands on
levels.note: The frame opens to five across, and nine pieces on a cross. Fifteen swaps land a match; one lands two.

levels.teaches: Most swaps pay once
levels.note: The cross opened into a diamond. Twenty-nine swaps land a match and the answer is still a single pair.

levels.teaches: The whole board is in reach, and one pair is the answer
levels.note: The frame full. A hundred and eighteen swaps land a match, and one pair pays twice.

levels.teaches: A points the way it pushes, and what it pushes lands home
levels.note: The column above the A is grounded so every piece it moves lands matched. The visible match clears one and loses the level.

levels.teaches: Turned over, it points the other way
levels.note: The same column and the same swap, with only the letter turned. Nothing else on the board changed.

levels.teaches: Two aims on one board, and only one of them pays
levels.note: Two A's facing apart down one column. No swap on this board shows two matches; eighteen show one, and one of those clears four.

levels.teaches: On its side it works across
levels.note: The sideways letter is never demonstrated. Forty-two swaps land a match; the ones showing two clear two, and the answer clears five.

levels.teaches: Which one you fire is the choice
levels.note: Four A's over a full frame, and a hundred and thirty-four swaps that land a match. The ones showing two clear two; the answer clears eight.

levels.teaches: O advances all four lines at once
levels.note: The O has to be carried onto its colour, and only an inner cell has all four arms on the board. Two of them run off the edge; two land home.

levels.teaches: A shoved glyph can land on its own colour — the chain
levels.note: Two O's. The first fires four arms and shoves the second onto its own colour, which fires in turn. Thirty-one swaps land a match.

levels.teaches: A pulse can shove an A onto its colour, and the A fires on
levels.note: The frame opens, and the O sits on the true centre a 4x4 has no room for. The answer empties the board.

levels.teaches: More board, and more swaps that look right
levels.note: The same chain on a diamond. Thirty-five swaps land a match; the ones showing two clear two.

levels.teaches: Three abilities in one swap
levels.note: A full frame, two O's and two A's. A hundred and thirty-two swaps land a match, and the answer runs pulse, push, pulse.

levels.teaches: A line stops at H, and what it stops behind lands home
levels.note: The shortest demonstration a 4x4 has room for: the front of the line is eaten at the wall, the piece behind it advances one and lands matched.

levels.teaches: H will not be shoved, and the arm that points at it does nothing
levels.note: A pulse with an anchor for one of its four neighbours. Three arms move; the fourth is refused before it starts.

levels.teaches: Aim into the wall on purpose
levels.note: One A and one H at the far end of its line. Seventeen swaps land a match and only the one that fires the A reaches the target.

levels.teaches: The wall is at the end of the only line that pays
levels.note: The same line on a diamond, with thirty-one swaps landing a match instead of seventeen.

levels.teaches: A wall on every row, and one of them dies
levels.note: Five anchors on the diagonal, so no line escapes one. A hundred and thirty swaps land a match; the answer moves an anchor onto its own colour and fires a pulse into the gap.

levels.teaches: + trades above with below, and left with right
levels.note: Every cell in the diamond is grounded for the piece the + sends to it.

levels.teaches: X trades the corners instead
levels.note: The mirror of the + board, on the corners.

levels.teaches: r turns the four around it one step clockwise
levels.note: Four cells, each grounded for the piece the turn brings it. The letters say which way it went.

levels.teaches: Its mirror turns them back
levels.note: The same board the other way, so only the letter decides where each piece lands.

levels.teaches: S opens a hole and everything falls inward
levels.note: Each arm is grounded for the piece the pull brings in.
